    Dune Meadows I: One-Way PERMANOVA

    dune-oneway.Rmd

    This vignette uses the vegan::dune plant-community data and its environmental data frame, vegan::dune.env, to test whether Bray–Curtis community composition differs among management categories.

    data(dune, package = "vegan")
data(dune.env, package = "vegan")

dim(dune)
#> [1] 20 30
table(dune.env$Management)
#> 
#> BF HF NM SF 
#>  3  5  6  6
bray <- vegdist(dune, method = "bray")

    Replication is unequal, so the balanced pairwise-distance engine is not valid. The projection engine handles unequal group sizes and states the unrestricted sample-label permutation scheme explicitly.

    set.seed(20260718)
dune_oneway <- permanova_oneway(
  distance = bray,
  group = dune.env$Management,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260718,
  engine = "projection"
)
dune_oneway
#> One-way PERMANOVA (projection engine)
#>      term df       ss        ms pseudo_f p_perm
#>     group  3 1.468592 0.4895306 2.767243  0.005
#>  Residual 16 2.830430 0.1769019       NA     NA
#>     Total 19 4.299022        NA       NA     NA

    For this supported one-way model, the observed pseudo-F agrees with vegan::adonis2() to numerical tolerance.

    vegan_oneway <- adonis2(
  bray ~ Management,
  data = dune.env,
  permutations = 0
)

c(
  distmer = dune_oneway$table$pseudo_f[1],
  vegan = vegan_oneway$F[1],
  absolute_difference = abs(dune_oneway$table$pseudo_f[1] - vegan_oneway$F[1])
)
#>             distmer               vegan absolute_difference 
#>        2.767243e+00        2.767243e+00        4.440892e-16

    The p-value belongs to this one-way, unrestricted-label null distribution. It must not be reused for a blocked, repeated, or mixed design.
